idiom_name: protocol port + adapter type + Decodable DTOs with throwing initialisers
implementation_notes: Swift expresses the boundary with a protocol the domain owns (protocol OrderPort { func place(_ order: Order) async throws -> Receipt }), a small adapter type that owns its URLSession client, boundary DTOs conforming to Decodable/Encodable with CodingKeys for foreign key names, and throwing initialisers that validate while converting (init(legacy: LegacyReceiptDTO) throws). What replaces the classic facade/adapter/translator classes is the protocol plus these value types and their initialisers; an explicit facade is justified when several upstream calls form one operation. Custom init(from:) is where unit, date and enum normalisation belong, so the domain never sees the wire shape.
pitfalls: Codable is not validation: Decodable accepts any well-formed JSON, so range, unit and enum invariants must be checked in the initialiser or the domain receives impossible values.
Enum decoding of upstream strings fails hard; model unknown cases explicitly (an unknown(String) case or a lenient init(from:)) instead of failing the whole payload.
URLSession is a reference type: a shared session shares cookies, credentials and caches across the boundary unless an ephemeral configuration is used.
Protocols with associated types erase awkwardly - keep the port existential-friendly (no Self or associated types) or the domain needs generics everywhere.
